title: An emerald in the sky
caption: Comet 252P/LINEAR over an Auxiliary Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: One of the Auxiliary Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope seems to point straight at a green, emerald-like glow high above it. That glow is Comet 252P/LINEAR.

The comet was discovered in April 2000 and has only fairly recently arrived in the inner Solar System, travelling between the orbits of Jupiter and Earth. In March 2016 it passed especially close to our planet, at only 5.2 million kilometres, which ranks it as the fifth closest comet passage ever recorded. At the time this picture was released, it could still be seen from the southern hemisphere.

Its green colour comes from carbon-based gas around the comet that fluoresces, glowing as it absorbs sunlight. Comets are icy bodies, and as they near the Sun they release gas and dust that can form a glowing cloud around them, as this one does.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the comet's green tint shows more strongly than it would to someone looking up.

explore: The picture was taken by ESO Photo Ambassador Babak A. Tafreshi at the start of ESO's Fulldome Expedition, a project to capture more pictures from ESO's observatories and of the southern night sky.
alt: An Auxiliary Telescope points toward a green, fuzzy comet high in a starry sky.
